questions.question: A and B working separately can complete a piece of work 60 days and 70 days, respectively. If they work for a day alternately, B beginning, in how many days will the work be completed?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(60, 70) = 420 units.

Efficiencies: A = 420 ÷ 60 = 7, B = 420 ÷ 70 = 6.

Work in 2 days (B + A) = 6 + 7 = 13 units.

Work in 32 pairs (64 days) = 32 × 13 = 416 units. Remaining = 420 − 416 = 4 units.

B completes the last 4 units in 4 ÷ 6 = 2/3 day.

Total time = 64 + 2/3 = 64 2/3 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 64 2/3 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A = 60 days

Time taken by B = 70 days

Sequence of work: B starts, then they work on alternate days (B, A, B, A, ...)

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 60
 420
 7
 
 

 B
 70
 6
 
 

⇒ Total work (LCM of 60 and 70) = 420 units.

⇒ Work done in 1st day (B) = 6 units.

⇒ Work done in 2nd day (A) = 7 units.

⇒ Total work in one cycle of 2 days = 6 + 7 = 13 units.

⇒ Total cycles = 420 ÷ 13 = 32 cycles with a remainder.

⇒ Work done in 32 cycles (64 days) = 32 × 13 = 416 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 420 − 416 = 4 units.

⇒ On the 65th day, it is B’s turn. B completes 4 units in = 4 ÷ 6 = 2/3 days.

⇒ Total time taken = 64 + 2/3 = 64 2/3 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 64 2/3 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alternate Day Working Rule

The total time taken depends on who starts the work. Calculate work done per cycle and identify whose turn it is for the remaining work.

Total Work via LCM

Total work is best assumed as the LCM of time taken by individuals. Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Individual Time.

Work and Wages

When workers are paid, the wages are distributed in the ratio of the total work done by each individual, not just their efficiency ratio.</p

questions.question: What will be the perimeter (in cm) of the sector of a circle of radius 4.9 cm having central angle 144° (use pi = (22)/(7))
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The perimeter of a sector consists of its arc length and two radii.

Arc length = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr = (144 ÷ 360) × 2 × (22 ÷ 7) × 4.9 = 12.32 cm

Perimeter = Arc length + 2 × r

⇒ Perimeter = 12.32 + 2 × 4.9 = 12.32 + 9.8 = 22.12 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 22.12 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/68fce97c77a4607cf5e2bcd8fe45fec866bf5454303df424bb5fb107004b994b.png] 

**Given:**

Radius of the sector (r) = 4.9 cm

Central angle (θ) = 144°

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter of a sector = Arc length (l) + 2r

Arc length (l) = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr

**Calculations:**

⇒ Arc length (l) = (144° ÷ 360°) × 2 × (22 ÷ 7) × 4.9

⇒ l = (2 ÷ 5) × 2 × 22 × 0.7

⇒ l = 0.4 × 30.8 = 12.32 cm

⇒ Perimeter of sector = l + 2r

⇒ Perimeter = 12.32 + 2 × 4.9

⇒ Perimeter = 12.32 + 9.8 = 22.12 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 22.12 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Sector

Area = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr². It represents the region enclosed by two radii and the corresponding arc.

Length of Arc

Arc length (l) = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr. It calculates the boundary length of the curved part of a sector.

Area of a Segment

The area enclosed between a chord and its corresponding arc. Area = Area of Sector − Area of Triangle.
</p

questions.question: Mother is four times the age of her son. If after 5 years, she would be three times of son’s age, then after 15 years, how many times she would be of her son’s age?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Mother (M) to Son (S) Now = 4 : 1 (Difference = 3 units)

Ratio after 5 years = 3 : 1 (Difference = 2 units)

Equalize difference: Now (8 : 2) and After 5 years (9 : 3). Difference is 6 units in both.

Increase of 1 unit = 5 years ⇒ Mother's current age = 8 × 5 = 40 years; Son = 2 × 5 = 10 years.

After 15 years: Mother = 40 + 15 = 55 years; Son = 10 + 15 = 25 years.

Required times = 55 ÷ 25 = 11/5.

**∴ The correct answer is 11/5 times.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Mother's age = 4 × Son's age

Formula: Age after n years = Current age + n

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9ccc7d8adacc5e7ccdf7b017ebde48481cc00eda7622f7a21961a520c831ca8c.png] 

Let current age of Son = x years

Mother's current age = 4x years

After 5 years:

⇒ (4x + 5) = 3 × (x + 5)

⇒ 4x + 5 = 3x + 15

⇒ 4x − 3x = 15 − 5

⇒ x = 10 years (Son's current age)

⇒ Mother's current age = 4 × 10 = 40 years

After 15 years:

⇒ Mother's age = 40 + 15 = 55 years

⇒ Son's age = 10 + 15 = 25 years

⇒ Ratio = 55 ÷ 25 = 11/5

**∴ The correct answer is 11/5 times.**

**__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two people remains constant regardless of the number of years passed or the ratio changes.

Ratio Balancing Method

To solve age problems quickly, multiply the ratios such that the numerical difference between the parts (M − S) becomes equal for all time periods.

Percentage in Ages

Sometimes ages are given in %, where 400% of son's age means 4 times. ⇒ % change = [(New Age − Old Age) ÷ Old Age] × 100.</p

questions.question: Find the sum (17)/(10)+(52)/(100)+(37)/(1000) in decimal form.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Expression = (17)/(10) + (52)/(100) + (37)/(1000)

**Formula used:**

Decimal conversion of fractions: (a)/(10^n) shifts decimal n places to the left.

**Calculations:**

(17)/(10) + (52)/(100) + (37)/(1000)

⇒ 1.7 + 0.52 + 0.037

⇒ 2.257

**∴ The correct answer is option (2).**

questions.question: A box containing the denominations of one rupee coins, two rupee coins and ten rupee coins amount to Rs. 2730. There are equal number of coins in all. Find the total number of coins in the box?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Sum of denominations = 1 + 2 + 10 = ₹13

Since the number of coins is equal, let there be 1 coin of each type in one set.

Number of such sets = Total Amount ÷ Sum of denominations

Number of sets = 2730 ÷ 13 = 210

Total coins = Number of sets × 3 types of coins = 210 × 3 = 630

**∴ The correct answer is 630 coins.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Denominations: ₹1, ₹2, and ₹10 coins.

Total Amount = ₹2730.

Condition: Number of coins for each denomination is equal.

**Formula Used:**

Total Value = (Denomination₁ × Number₁) + (Denomination₂ × Number₂) + ...

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c26d314585aca0642ba3cc8a5a71249e55e4797c4158063e6b4942f0f3ed9343.png] 

Let the number of coins of each denomination be x.

⇒ Total Amount = (1 × x) + (2 × x) + (10 × x)

⇒ 2730 = 1x + 2x + 10x

⇒ 2730 = 13x

⇒ x = 2730 ÷ 13

⇒ x = 210

⇒ Since there are three types of coins, total number of coins = x + x + x

⇒ Total coins = 3x = 3 × 210

⇒ Total coins = 630

**∴ The correct answer is 630 coins.**

**__Additional Information__**

Coin Value Relationship

Ratio of value of coins = (Ratio of number of coins) × (Ratio of their respective face values).

Ratio and Proportion in Currency

If number of coins of denominations D₁, D₂ are in ratio a:b, then their value ratio is (a×D₁) : (b×D₂).

Total Amount Calculation

Total Value = ∑ (Denominationᵢ × Number of coinsᵢ). To find the number of coins when the value is given, divide the total value by the weighted sum of denominations.

questions.question: Two friends started for a place one by motorcycle and the other by train. The speed of motorcycle is 30 km/h and that of train is 24 km/h. The first one takes 6 h 12 min to reach the destination. Find the time of reaching of second one.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed ratio (Motorcycle : Train) = 30 : 24 = 5 : 4

As distance is constant, Time ratio = 1/5 : 1/4 = 4 : 5

Motorcycle time = 6 h 12 min = 6 + 12/60 = 6.2 h

4 units = 6.2 h ⇒ 1 unit = 1.55 h

Train time (5 units) = 5 × 1.55 = 7.75 h

**∴ The correct answer is 7.75 h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of Motorcycle (S₁) = 30 km/h

Speed of Train (S₂) = 24 km/h

Time taken by Motorcycle (T₁) = 6 h 12 min

**Formula Used:**

Distance (D) = Speed × Time

For constant distance: S₁ × T₁ = S₂ × T₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/93b1a4bddbb0d771fef8841fe23a68fea348c247f9655288a2a1ceb2e3610cf0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Convert T₁ to hours: 6 h + (12 ÷ 60) h = 6 + 0.2 = 6.2 h

⇒ Total Distance (D) = S₁ × T₁ = 30 × 6.2

⇒ D = 186 km

⇒ Time taken by Train (T₂) = Distance ÷ Speed₂

⇒ T₂ = 186 ÷ 24

⇒ T₂ = 7.75 h

**∴ The correct answer is 7.75 h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportionality Rule

When the distance is constant, speed and time are inversely proportional to each other: S₁/S₂ = T₂/T₁.

Conversion of Time Units

To convert minutes into hours, divide the value by 60. Example: 45 min = 45/60 = 0.75 hours.

Basic Relation

Speed = Distance ÷ Time. To find any one variable, the other two must be known or their relationship must be established.</p

questions.question: Let P and Q be two towers with the same base. Exactly midway between the foot of the two towers P and Q, the angels of elevation of their tops are 30º and 60º, respectively.The ratio of the heights of Q to P is :
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For two objects at equal distance from an observation point, the ratio of their heights is the ratio of the tangents of their angles of elevation.

Height of Q : Height of P = tan 60° : tan 30°

Ratio = √3 : (1/√3)

Ratio = (√3 × √3) : 1 = 3 : 1

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 1.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Midway point M between foot of tower P and tower Q. Angles of elevation θP = 30° and θQ = 60°.

Formula: tan θ = Height / Distance

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/02d3d1a6cb2a90d93fb2e4f2f8b6f4055c72b3b22b0ee1c9690b59dd4524eceb.png] 

Let the distance from midpoint M to each tower base be d.

⇒ In triangle for tower P: tan 30° = HeightP / d

⇒ HeightP = d × (1/√3)

⇒ In triangle for tower Q: tan 60° = HeightQ / d

⇒ HeightQ = d × √3

⇒ Ratio Q : P = HeightQ / HeightP = (d × √3) / (d / √3)

⇒ Ratio = √3 × √3 = 3 / 1

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 1.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

Key values: tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3. These are derived from right-angled triangle properties.

Angle of Elevation

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when looking up at an object. It is equal to the angle of depression from the top of the object to the observer.

Proportionality Rule

When the base distance is constant, height (h) is directly proportional to the tangent of the angle of elevation (θ). Formula: h₁/h₂ = tan θ₁ / tan θ₂.</p

questions.question: If on an item a company gives 25% discount, they earn 25% profit. If they give 10% discount then what is the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct relation: CP/MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%)

From Case 1: CP/MP = (100 − 25) / (100 + 25) = 75 / 125 = 3 / 5

In Case 2: 3 / 5 = (100 − 10) / (100 + P) ⇒ 3 / 5 = 90 / (100 + P)

Cross multiplying: 100 + P = (90 × 5) ÷ 3 = 150

Profit = 150 − 100 = 50%

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Case 1: Discount₁ = 25%, Profit₁ = 25%

Case 2: Discount₂ = 10%, Find Profit₂%

**Formula Used:**

CP/MP = (100 − D%) / (100 + P%)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a5fb187b9853ff7f53a231bda7a5549271b823bc638343185dc57866799ae4d9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ In the first case, CP / MP = (100 − 25) / (100 + 25)

⇒ CP / MP = 75 / 125 = 3 / 5

⇒ Let Cost Price (CP) = 300 and Marked Price (MP) = 500

⇒ New Discount = 10% of MP = 10% of 500 = 50

⇒ New Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount = 500 − 50 = 450

⇒ New Profit = SP − CP = 450 − 300 = 150

⇒ Profit % = (Profit / CP) × 100 = (150 / 300) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 50%

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

CP and MP Relationship

The ratio of Cost Price to Marked Price is always given by CP / MP = (100 − D%) / (100 + P%). This is the fastest way to bridge CP and MP without finding SP.

Markup Percentage

Markup % = (MP − CP) / CP × 100. It represents how much the price is increased above the cost price before offering a discount.

Successive Discounts

If two discounts x% and y% are given, the equivalent single discount is [x + y − (x × y) / 100] %.</p

questions.question: A man sold his cycle at 17% loss. If he had sold it for Rs. 1,056 more, he would have made 5% profit, The cost price of the cycle is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total percentage gap = Loss% + Profit% (since signs are opposite).

Gap = 17% + 5% = 22%.

Given that 22% of CP = ₹1,056.

Cost Price (100%) = (1,056 ÷ 22) × 100.

CP = 48 × 100 = ₹4,800.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Loss percentage = 17%

Profit percentage = 5%

Difference in Selling Price = ₹1,056

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 − Loss)%

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Profit)%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4586f5125a1a726f64eb75c23f8aa0cb873f018b636498179afcbcafedae6424.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) of the cycle be ₹x.

⇒ First Selling Price (SP₁) = x × (100 − 17)/100 = 0.83x

⇒ Second Selling Price (SP₂) = x × (100 + 5)/100 = 1.05x

⇒ According to the question: SP₂ − SP₁ = 1,056

⇒ 1.05x − 0.83x = 1,056

⇒ 0.22x = 1,056

⇒ x = 1,056 ÷ 0.22

⇒ x = 1,05,600 ÷ 22

⇒ x = 4,800

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Difference Rule

When moving from a loss to a profit, the effective percentage change is the sum of the loss and profit percentages: CP = (Price Difference) ÷ (Profit% + Loss%) × 100.

Basic Profit and Loss Relation

Profit = SP − CP and Loss = CP − SP. Both percentages are always calculated on the Cost Price unless specified otherwise.

Successive Percentage Change

If an item is sold through multiple hands, the final price is CP × (1 ± r₁/100) × (1 ± r₂/100) where r represents the profit/loss rate at each stage.

questions.question: Three fair coins are tossed simultaneously. Find the probability of getting one head.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total outcomes for 3 fair coins = 2³ = 8.

Possible outcomes for exactly one head are: HTT, THT, TTH.

Number of favorable outcomes = 3.

Required Probability = Favorable outcomes ÷ Total outcomes = 3/8.

**∴ The correct answer is 3/8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 3 fair coins are tossed.

**Formula Used:** Probability P(E) = n(E) ÷ n(S)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6a0fc54ba55358f9bb7b59953061ee04d9d27a1b2b4b108e8c69a0ccf4c4ce85.png] 

⇒ Sample Space S = {HHH, HHT, HTH, THH, HTT, THT, TTH, TTT}

⇒ Total number of outcomes, n(S) = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8

⇒ Let E be the event of getting exactly one head.

⇒ Favorable outcomes, E = {HTT, THT, TTH}

⇒ Number of favorable outcomes, n(E) = 3

⇒ Probability P(E) = n(E) ÷ n(S) = 3/8

**∴ The correct answer is 3/8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Outcomes of n Coins

When n fair coins are tossed, the total number of possible outcomes is always 2ⁿ.

Binomial Probability

The number of ways to get exactly 'r' heads in 'n' tosses is given by the combination formula ⁿCᵣ = n! ÷ (r! × (n−r)!). Here, ³C₁ = 3! ÷ (1! × 2!) = 3.

Complementary Events

The probability of an event E not occurring is P(E') = 1 − P(E). For example, P(at least one head) = 1 − P(no heads) = 1 − 1/8 = 7/8.</p

questions.question: The time taken by a boat to cover a certain distance upstream is equal to 4/7 of the time taken by it to cover three times the same distance downstream. The speed of the stream is 7.5 km/h. How many (total) hours will the boat take to go 42 km upstream and 54 km downstream?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time ratio for same distance (Upstream : Downstream) = 4 : (7 ÷ 3) = 12 : 7

Speed ratio (Upstream : Downstream) = 7 : 12 (Inverse of time ratio)

Ratio of stream speed = (12 − 7) ÷ 2 = 2.5 units

2.5 units = 7.5 km/h ⇒ 1 unit = 3 km/h

Upstream Speed = 21 km/h | Downstream Speed = 36 km/h

Total time = (42 ÷ 21) + (54 ÷ 36) = 2 + 1.5 = 3.5 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 3.5 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance Upstream (Dᵤ) = d | Distance Downstream (Dd) = 3d

Time Upstream (Tᵤ) = 4/7 × Time Downstream (Td)

Speed of stream (v) = 7.5 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f843d940198e1a74890b626a6640d957552aca6167c3bfc2601b3b9684285cfb.png] 

Let speed of boat in still water be x km/h.

⇒ Upstream speed (u) = (x − 7.5) km/h

⇒ Downstream speed (d) = (x + 7.5) km/h

⇒ Tᵤ = d ÷ (x − 7.5) and Td = 3d ÷ (x + 7.5)

⇒ d ÷ (x − 7.5) = 4/7 × [3d ÷ (x + 7.5)]

⇒ 1 ÷ (x − 7.5) = 12 ÷ [7 × (x + 7.5)]

⇒ 7x + 52.5 = 12x − 90

⇒ 5x = 142.5 ⇒ x = 28.5 km/h

⇒ u = 28.5 − 7.5 = 21 km/h | d = 28.5 + 7.5 = 36 km/h

⇒ Total Time = (42 ÷ 21) + (54 ÷ 36)

⇒ Total Time = 2 + 1.5 = 3.5 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 3.5 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Boat and Stream Speed Relations

Speed of Boat in Still Water (x) = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2

Speed of Stream

Speed of Stream (v) = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2

Average Speed for Round Trip

Average Speed = (Upstream Speed × Downstream Speed) ÷ Speed of boat in still water (x) when distance is same.</p

questions.question: In ΔPQR, side QR is produced to S. RT is drawn parallel to QP. If ∠PRT = 68° and ∠PQR = 35°, then what is the difference between the angles QRP and TRS?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since RT || QP, corresponding angles ∠TRS = ∠PQR = 35°.

Alternate interior angles ∠QPR = ∠PRT = 68°.

In ΔPQR, ∠QRP = 180° − (35° + 68°) = 77°.

Difference = |∠QRP − ∠TRS| = 77° − 35° = 42°.

**∴ The correct answer is 42°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

∠PRT = 68°, ∠PQR = 35°, RT || QP, and QR is produced to S.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b817565f1bdf421bc8574a3080f4f2677a56a111e7635fa40de224a09ef19d98.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ RT || QP and QS is the transversal.

⇒ ∠TRS = ∠PQR (Corresponding angles)

⇒ ∠TRS = 35°

⇒ RT || QP and PR is the transversal.

⇒ ∠QPR = ∠PRT (Alternate interior angles)

⇒ ∠QPR = 68°

⇒ In ΔPQR: ∠PQR + ∠QPR + ∠QRP = 180°

⇒ 35° + 68° + ∠QRP = 180°

⇒ 103° + ∠QRP = 180°

⇒ ∠QRP = 180° − 103° = 77°

⇒ Difference = ∠QRP − ∠TRS

⇒ Difference = 77° − 35° = 42°

**∴ The correct answer is 42°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Parallel Lines Properties

When two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, corresponding angles are equal and alternate interior angles are equal.

Exterior Angle Theorem

The exterior angle of a triangle (∠PRS) is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles (∠PQR + ∠QPR).

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all interior angles of a triangle is always 180°.</p

questions.question: The average of six consecutive odd numbers is 68. What is the cube of the difference between the highest and the lowest numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any n consecutive odd or even numbers, the difference between the highest and lowest number is always (n − 1) × 2.

Here, n = 6 numbers, so the Difference = (6 − 1) × 2 = 10.

The average value (68) does not affect the difference between the terms.

Required value = Cube of the difference = 10³ = 1000.

**∴ The correct answer is 1000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average of 6 consecutive odd numbers = 68

**Formula Used:**

Average of consecutive numbers in AP = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7afb80a127d7399c1129af2b17d989b5c85d69f9747d4c5b5742f91f0ecc7f20.png] 

For an even number of terms (6), the average lies exactly between the two middle terms.

⇒ Middle terms (3rd and 4th) = 68 − 1 and 68 + 1

⇒ 3rd term = 67, 4th term = 69

⇒ Full sequence of odd numbers: 63, 65, 67, 69, 71, 73

⇒ Lowest number = 63

⇒ Highest number = 73

⇒ Difference = 73 − 63 = 10

⇒ Cube of difference = 10³ = 10 × 10 × 10 = 1000

**∴ The correct answer is 1000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of Arithmetic Progression (AP)

For any sequence in AP, the average is the middle term (if n is odd) or the mean of the two middle terms (if n is even).

Difference between Extreme Terms

In a sequence of n terms with common difference d, the difference between the nth and 1st term is (n − 1) × d.

Sum of Consecutive Odd Numbers

The sum of the first n odd natural numbers starting from 1 is always n².</p

questions.question: If 2a - 3b : 5a + 4b = 1 : 7, then (a - b) is equal to
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given: (2a − 3b) / (5a + 4b) = 1 / 7

Cross multiply: 14a − 21b = 5a + 4b

Combine like terms: 14a − 5a = 21b + 4b ⇒ 9a = 25b

Express in terms of constant k: a/25 = b/9 = k ⇒ a = 25k and b = 9k

Required value: a − b = 25k − 9k = 16k

**∴ The correct answer is 16 × constant.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio (2a − 3b) : (5a + 4b) = 1 : 7

**Formula Used:**

If x : y = m : n, then x/y = m/n. Ratio constant k where a = xk and b = yk.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bcc9b553b0693823223020a7ebac509c1481d1f6112acd2eb75ab12a48e74a2d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (2a − 3b) / (5a + 4b) = 1 / 7

⇒ 7 × (2a − 3b) = 1 × (5a + 4b)

⇒ 14a − 21b = 5a + 4b

⇒ 14a − 5a = 21b + 4b

⇒ 9a = 25b

⇒ a / b = 25 / 9

⇒ Let a = 25k and b = 9k, where k is a constant.

⇒ a − b = 25k − 9k

⇒ a − b = 16k

**∴ The correct answer is 16 × constant.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Componendo and Dividendo Rule

If a/b = c/d, then (a + b) / (a − b) = (c + d) / (c − d). This rule helps in simplifying complex ratio equations quickly.

Duplicate and Sub-duplicate Ratio

The duplicate ratio of a : b is a² : b², and the sub-duplicate ratio is √a : √b.

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is given by x = √(a × b), such that a : x = x : b.</p

questions.question: If 2x² + 5x + 1 = 0, then one of the values of x - (1)/({2x)} is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Divide the equation 2x² + 5x + 1 = 0 by 2x to find x + 1/(2x) = −5/2.

Use the direct relationship (x − 1/2x)² = (x + 1/2x)² − 2.

Calculation: (−5/2)² − 2 = 25/4 − 2 = 17/4.

Taking square root: x − 1/2x = √17 / 2.

**∴ The correct answer is √17 / 2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 2x² + 5x + 1 = 0

**Formula Used:** (a − b)² = (a + b)² − 4ab

⇒ 2x² + 1 = −5x

⇒ (2x² + 1) / 2x = −5x / 2x

⇒ x + 1/(2x) = −5/2

Now, to find x − 1/(2x), square both sides of the identity:

⇒ (x − 1/(2x))² = (x + 1/(2x))² − 4 × x × (1/2x)

⇒ (x − 1/(2x))² = (−5/2)² − 2

⇒ (x − 1/(2x))² = 25/4 − 2

⇒ (x − 1/(2x))² = (25 − 8) / 4 = 17 / 4

⇒ x − 1/(2x) = ±√(17 / 4)

⇒ x − 1/(2x) = √17 / 2 (taking positive value)

**∴ The correct answer is √17 / 2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity for Reciprocals

For any value k, if x + 1/x = k, then (x − 1/x)² = k² − 4.

Quadratic Formula

For ax² + bx + c = 0, the roots are x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / 2a.

Square of a Sum and Difference

(a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab is a fundamental identity used to convert between sums and differences.</p

questions.question: A boy covers a certain distance between his house and school on a cycle. Having an average speed of 10 km/h, he is late by 10 min. However, with an average speed of 15 km/h, he reaches the school in 5 min. earlier. Find the distance (in km) between his house and school.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Speed ratio = 10 : 15 → 2 : 3

Since distance is constant, Time ratio = 3 : 2

Difference in time = 3 − 2 = 1 unit → 10 min + 5 min = 15 min

Time taken at 10 km/h = 3 units = 3 × 15 = 45 min = 3/4 hour

Distance = Speed × Time = 10 × 3/4 = 7.5 km

**∴ The correct answer is 7.5 km.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed 1 (S₁) = 10 km/h, Late time = 10 min

Speed 2 (S₂) = 15 km/h, Early time = 5 min

**Formula Used:**

Distance = [(S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₂ − S₁)] × (Total time difference in hours)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c83a4814f866ccec61db559eb15f353a99e90194992758bef6fd7df5a5a3682f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total time difference = 10 min − (−5 min) = 15 min

⇒ Time difference in hours = 15 ÷ 60 = 1/4 hr

⇒ Distance = [(10 × 15) ÷ (15 − 10)] × 1/4

⇒ Distance = [150 ÷ 5] × 1/4

⇒ Distance = 30 × 1/4

⇒ Distance = 7.5 km

**∴ The correct answer is 7.5 km.**

**__Additional Information__**

Speed-Time Relationship

When distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S ∝ 1/T). If speed ratio is a:b, time ratio is b:a.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed Formula

When a person covers equal distances at speeds x and y, the average speed for the whole journey is (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).</p

questions.question: If the simple interest on a sum of money at 5% per annum for 3 years is Rs. 1,200, then what will be the compound interest on the same amount at the same rate for the same period?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Simple interest for 1 year = 1,200 ÷ 3 = ₹400.

Interest on 1st year interest (5% of 400) = ₹20.

Interest on that interest (5% of 20) = ₹1.

Compound interest (3 years) = 3 × (400) + 3 × (20) + 1 × (1) = 1,200 + 60 + 1 = ₹1,261.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,261.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Simple Interest (SI) = ₹1,200, Rate (R) = 5% p.a., Time (T) = 3 years.

**Formula Used:** SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100; CI = P[(1 + R/100)T − 1]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/23cf192f489b97873100e839b59dd2414a0832dbc5e377aefbc8a58e12a103c5.png] 

⇒ 1,200 = (P × 5 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ 1,200 = 15P ÷ 100

⇒ P = (1,200 × 100) ÷ 15 = ₹8,000

⇒ CI = 8,000[(1 + 5/100)³ − 1]

⇒ CI = 8,000[(21/20)³ − 1]

⇒ CI = 8,000[9,261/8,000 − 1]

⇒ CI = 8,000 × (1,261/8,000) = ₹1,261.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,261.**

**__Additional Information__**

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years

The difference is given by the formula: D = PR² ÷ 100².

Difference between CI and SI for 3 years

The difference is given by the formula: D = [PR²(300 + R)] ÷ 100³.

Effective Rate of CI

For a rate of r% for 3 years, the effective rate is [3r + 3r²/100 + r³/10000]%. For 5%, it is 15.7625%.

questions.question: The marked price of an article is 25 percent more than its cost price. What is the maximum discount percentage at which the shopkeeper sells his article with no profit or no loss?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of CP : MP = 100 : 125 = 4 : 5.

For no profit/loss, SP must be equal to CP, so SP = 4 units.

Discount allowed = MP − SP = 5 − 4 = 1 unit.

Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100 = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Markup % = 25%

Condition = No profit or loss (SP = CP)

**Formula Used:**

Discount % = [(MP − SP) ÷ MP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/31c759cfa518c1f3afcfa8836f55064a51b00845abf53d14b1ab802049e9db75.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Cost Price (CP) of the article = ₹100

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = CP + 25% of CP = 100 + 25 = ₹125

⇒ Since there is no profit and no loss, Selling Price (SP) = CP = ₹100

⇒ Discount = Marked Price − Selling Price

⇒ Discount = 125 − 100 = ₹25

⇒ Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100

⇒ Discount % = (25 ÷ 125) × 100

⇒ Discount % = 1/5 × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Markup Percentage

Markup % is the percentage by which the CP is increased to get the MP. MP = CP × [1 + (Markup% ÷ 100)].

Relationship between Markup, Discount and Profit

Net Profit% = Markup% − Discount% − [(Markup% × Discount%) ÷ 100]. If Profit = 0, then Markup% − Discount% = (Markup% × Discount%) ÷ 100.

Discount Calculation

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). SP = MP × [1 − (Discount% ÷ 100)].

questions.question: What is the remainder when 3255 is divided by 28?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert the base 3 to a power close to the divisor 28: 3³ = 27.

Rewrite the expression: 3²⁵⁵ = (3³)⁸⁵ = 27⁸⁵.

Since 27 is 1 less than 28, the remainder is (−1)⁸⁵ = −1.

Final positive remainder = 28 − 1 = 27.

**∴ The correct answer is 27.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Dividend = 3²⁵⁵, Divisor = 28

**Formula Used:** Remainder of (a − 1)ⁿ ÷ a is (−1)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/61bb18e999503ea54d5e02ea71f9a41f928cbabe8b7cb0e02246e56c87124947.png] 

⇒ 3²⁵⁵ = (3³)⁸⁵

⇒ 3³ = 27

⇒ Remainder [3²⁵⁵ ÷ 28] = Remainder [27⁸⁵ ÷ 28]

⇒ 27 ≡ −1 (mod 28)

⇒ Remainder = (−1)⁸⁵ = −1

⇒ Positive Remainder = 28 + (−1) = 27

**∴ The correct answer is 27.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Remainder Theorem for Powers

If a number (a + k)ⁿ is divided by a, the remainder is kⁿ. In this case, (28 − 1)⁸⁵ divided by 28 leaves (−1)⁸⁵.

Negative Remainder Property

A negative remainder −r is equivalent to a positive remainder (Divisor − r). It is a useful intermediate step to simplify calculations.

Odd and Even Powers of −1

(−1)ⁿ = 1 if n is even, and (−1)ⁿ = −1 if n is odd. This rule determines the sign of the intermediate remainder.</p

questions.question: In a equilateral triangle ΔABC, the interior angle bisector for ∠B and exterior angle bisector for ∠C meets at E. Find the ∠BEC.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The angle formed by the intersection of an interior angle bisector of one vertex and the exterior angle bisector of another vertex is always half of the third angle of the triangle.

Formula: ∠BEC = (1/2) × ∠A

Since ΔABC is an equilateral triangle, all interior angles are 60°.

∴ ∠A = 60°

∠BEC = 60° ÷ 2 = 30°

**∴ The correct answer is 30°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ΔABC is equilateral, ∠B interior bisector and ∠C exterior bisector meet at E.

**Formula Used:** Interior angles of equilateral triangle = 60°; Sum of angles in a triangle = 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8003f07d4fd16b4bd885f9f3aab8d7db7dd0ea4a4614655276fa671a8d411a52.png] 

⇒ In equilateral ΔABC, ∠ABC = ∠BCA = ∠BAC = 60°.

⇒ ∠EBC is the interior bisector of ∠ABC ⇒ ∠EBC = 60° ÷ 2 = 30°.

⇒ Exterior ∠ACD = 180° − ∠BCA = 180° − 60° = 120°.

⇒ ∠ACE is the exterior bisector of ∠ACD ⇒ ∠ACE = 120° ÷ 2 = 60°.

⇒ ∠BCE = ∠BCA + ∠ACE = 60° + 60° = 120°.

⇒ In ΔBCE, ∠EBC + ∠BCE + ∠BEC = 180°.

⇒ 30° + 120° + ∠BEC = 180°.

⇒ ∠BEC = 180° − 150° = 30°.

**∴ The correct answer is 30°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Incenter Properties

The intersection of all three interior angle bisectors is the incenter. The angle formed at the incenter I is ∠BIC = 90° + ∠A/2.

Excenter Properties

The intersection of two exterior angle bisectors is the excenter. The angle formed at the excenter E is ∠BEC = 90° − ∠A/2.

Exterior Angle Theorem

The exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles. ∠ACD = ∠BAC + ∠ABC.</p

questions.question: What is the total area of three equilateral triangles inscribed in a semicircle of radius 2 cm?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Side (a) of three equilateral triangles inscribed in a semicircle is equal to its radius (R).

Given: Radius (R) = 2 cm ⇒ Side (a) = 2 cm.

Total Area = 3 × Area of one equilateral triangle = 3 × [(√3 ÷ 4) × a²].

Total Area = 3 × (√3 ÷ 4) × 2² = 3 × √3 = 3√3 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 3√3 cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the semicircle (R) = 2 cm

Number of equilateral triangles = 3

**Formula Used:**

Area of an equilateral triangle = (√3 ÷ 4) × (side)²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/35e382f5ff08f97027f3b3d2480cf13563df8936eb673b88b2e3f594097574e2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ In a semicircle of 180°, three equilateral triangles (60° each) perfectly fit around the center.

⇒ The distance from the center to the vertices on the arc is the radius (R).

⇒ Therefore, the side of each equilateral triangle (a) = Radius (R) = 2 cm.

⇒ Area of one triangle = (√3 ÷ 4) × 2² = √3 cm².

⇒ Total Area of three triangles = 3 × √3 = 3√3 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 3√3 cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Area of Semicircle

The total area of a semicircle with radius R is given by A = 1÷2 × π × R².

Regular Hexagon Relation

Three equilateral triangles placed side-by-side in a semicircle form exactly half of a regular hexagon with the same side length.

Equilateral Triangle Height

The altitude or height (h) of an equilateral triangle with side a is h = (√3 ÷ 2) × a.</p

questions.question: The value of {(281 + 119)² - (281 - 119)²} over 281 times 119 is equal to which of the following?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

This expression is based on the algebraic identity: (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab.

Here, let a = 281 and b = 119.

The numerator simplifies directly to 4 × 281 × 119.

The denominator is given as 281 × 119.

Therefore, the expression becomes (4 × 281 × 119) ÷ (281 × 119) = 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: a = 281, b = 119

Method: Expansion of algebraic identities

⇒ Given Expression = ((281 + 119)² − (281 − 119)²) ÷ (281 × 119)

⇒ Let a = 281 and b = 119, then the expression is ((a + b)² − (a − b)²) ÷ (ab)

⇒ Expanding (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

⇒ Expanding (a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab

⇒ Numerator = (a² + b² + 2ab) − (a² + b² − 2ab) = 4ab

⇒ Expression = 4ab ÷ ab = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

**__Additional Information__**

Sum of Squares Identity

The sum of the square of the sum and the square of the difference is given by: (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²).

Difference of Squares

The formula a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b) is frequently used in simplification to factorize quadratic terms.

BODMAS Rule

Always follow the Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction order for multi-step calculations.</p

questions.question: A sum of money doubles itself at compound interest in 10 years. In how many years will it be four times at the same rate of interest?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In Compound Interest, if a sum becomes 'n' times in 'T' years, it becomes 'nk' times in 'k × T' years.

Here, the sum doubles (2 times) in 10 years (n = 2, T = 10).

To become four times (4 = 2²), the power k = 2.

Time required = k × T = 2 × 10 = 20 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Sum = P

Amount after 10 years = 2P

Target Amount = 4P

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 + r/100)t

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e36ae2a959de069380b62e30ec5538143e6b211b4a1e20a7f6b60d6ddc39ece2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2P = P(1 + r/100)¹⁰

⇒ 2 = (1 + r/100)¹⁰ ---- (i)

⇒ Let the required time be 't' years for the sum to become 4P.

⇒ 4P = P(1 + r/100)t

⇒ 4 = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ (2)² = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ Substituting value of 2 from (i):

⇒ [(1 + r/100)¹⁰]² = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ (1 + r/100)²⁰ = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ By comparing powers, t = 20 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate of Interest

When interest is compounded more than once a year, the effective annual rate is (1 + r/n)ⁿ − 1, where n is the frequency of compounding.

Rule of 72

A quick way to estimate how long it takes to double money at CI: Time ≈ 72 ÷ Interest Rate.

SI vs CI for Doubling

In Simple Interest, if a sum doubles in T years, it becomes n times in (n−1) × T years. For 4 times, it would take (4−1) × 10 = 30 years.</p

questions.question: In a lead pipe 4.2 m long, the external diameter is 5.4 cm and the thickness of the pipe is 3 mm. Find the weight of the pipe, if 1 cm³ of lead mass is 25 grams. (Use π = 22/7 )
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert all units to cm: Length (h) = 420 cm, R = 2.7 cm, r = (2.7 − 0.3) = 2.4 cm.

Using Volume of Hollow Cylinder = π × (R + r) × (R − r) × h

Volume = (22/7) × (2.7 + 2.4) × (2.7 − 2.4) × 420 = 22 × 60 × 5.1 × 0.3 = 2019.6 cm³.

Weight = (Volume × Density) / 1000 = (2019.6 × 25) / 1000 = 2019.6 / 40 = 50.49 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 50.49 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of pipe (h) = 4.2 m = 420 cm

External diameter (D) = 5.4 cm ⇒ External radius (R) = 2.7 cm

Thickness (t) = 3 mm = 0.3 cm

Density of lead = 25 g/cm³

Internal radius (r) = R − t = 2.7 − 0.3 = 2.4 cm

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/acd11433b61d52139dfb89287e725fa4bfad684b71948d7f64c4ce6983a7141a.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Volume of material in a hollow cylinder = πh(R² − r²)

Total Weight = Volume × Density

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 420 × (2.7² − 2.4²)

⇒ Volume = 22 × 60 × (7.29 − 5.76)

⇒ Volume = 1320 × 1.53

⇒ Volume = 2019.6 cm³

⇒ Weight of pipe in grams = 2019.6 × 25 = 50490 g

⇒ Weight in kg = 50490 / 1000 = 50.49 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 50.49 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of Hollow Cylinder

It is the difference between the volumes of the outer and inner cylinders: V = πR²h − πr²h = πh(R² − r²).

Total Surface Area of Hollow Cylinder

TSA = Outer CSA + Inner CSA + 2 × Area of Base Ring = 2πRh + 2πrh + 2π(R² − r²).

Mass and Density Relation
